props.description: Which form shows at each window class, or none, such as `{ compact: 'none' }` for an application that opens its navigation from the top bar on a phone. Where the form a window class asks for wasn't given, the nearest given form shows: a rail for a drawer and the other way round, then the bar.

props.name: topBarSpan
props.description: body: the top bar sits above the body, beside the rail or drawer, which run the full height. full: the top bar runs across the whole width, above the navigation, as a window's title bar must.

props.name: scroll
props.description: What scrolls. document: the page, as on any website, so a phone collapses its address bar, pull to refresh and a tap on the status bar work and the browser restores the scroll position; the top bar and the bar stick to the window's edges and the rail or the drawer stays in view, in a Scaffold at least as tall as the window. body: the body alone, under the top bar, in a Scaffold that fills its container's height, 100dvh unless a class gives it another, with the keyboard scrolling the body as it would the document: for a preview or an embedded frame, a window with its own title bar, or a body of Panes whose panes scroll on their own.

props.name: bodyId
props.default: 'main', or an id of its own where `landmarks` is false
props.description: The body's id, the target of the skip link to the content.

props.name: bodyRef
props.description: The body's element: with `scroll="body"` the element that scrolls, to read or restore its scroll position on.

props.name: skipToContentLabel
props.description: The name of the skip link to the body.

props.name: skipToNavigationLabel
props.description: The name of the skip link to the navigation.

props.name: landmarks
props.description: false renders the regions without landmarks, a div for the banner and the main, and no skip links, for a preview of an application inside another page's main content.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "app", which dev mode and the docs show; it renders as `data-env-name`.

props.name: children
props.description: The body: the page's main content, usually a Page or Panes.

SearchField.description: A search input with a search icon and, while it has a query, a clear button; Esc also clears. Its label is hidden by default, so it sits beside buttons with a placeholder.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's accessible name, such as Search members. It shows as a floating label only with showLabel; otherwise a placeholder gives the visible guidance.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label in the field, as TextField does. A search field leaves it out, so that it sits in a toolbar with a placeholder such as Search.

props.name: value
props.description: The query of a controlled field; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The query an uncontrolled field starts with, and that a form reset restores.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the next query as people type, and an empty string when the clear button or Esc clears it.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The accessible name and tooltip of the clear button.

props.name: placeholder
props.default: 'Search' while the label is hidden, or EnvUIProvider's messages.searchField.placeholder
props.description: The visible guidance while the field is empty, such as Search members. With the label hidden it shows Search unless it is set.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native input, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-text-field.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text before the value, such as the start of an address. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

props.name: size
props.description: The control height, sm, md or lg; without it, the container's, and else md. sm is for a field with its label hidden.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look: outline, a thin border its label floats into, or ghost, a faint fill, for a search at the top of a sidebar or a list.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text after the value, such as a unit. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

SegmentedControl.description: One choice among a few items, such as views or filters of the same content: segments in a recessed track, the chosen one raised on a thumb. A radio group, with one tab stop and arrow keys.

props.name: items
props.description: The items, two to five, in the order they show.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen item's value, for a control the application keeps; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The item an uncontrolled control starts with chosen.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the item people choose, by pressing it or with the arrow keys.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The group's accessible name, such as Work items; the control has no visible label.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale, so it lines up with buttons and fields of the same size. Without it, it takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the available width, split evenly between the items; a label too long for its share is cut short with an ellipsis and shows whole in a tooltip. Without it the control is as wide as its items, and scrolls in a container too narrow for them.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every item; the control can't be focused or changed.

Select.description: One choice from a list that stays collapsed until opened: an outlined field, as TextField is, whose button shows the chosen option and opens a popup list, where a check mark shows the chosen option, with its label inside, a description, an error and native form participation.

props.name: ref
props.description: The trigger, the button that shows the chosen option and opens the list.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-select.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element.

props.name: items
props.description: The options of the list, in order, each with a value, a label, an optional description and whether it is disabled.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen option's value in a controlled select, or null for none, which shows the placeholder; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The chosen option's value an uncontrolled select starts with; a native form reset returns to it. Without it, nothing is chosen and the trigger shows the placeholder.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the option people choose.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the list is open, for a select the application controls with onOpenChange.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the list of an uncontrolled select starts open, such as in a picture of the open list.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Receives the requested state, and why, each time the list asks to open or close.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: People can read the chosen option, and a form submits it, but the list doesn't open.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the chosen option's value with a form under this name, through a hidden input.

props.name: required
props.description: Require a choice before the form submits: the browser refuses the form and moves focus to the trigger while nothing is chosen.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: What the trigger shows while nothing is chosen, such as Choose an owner.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: A hint for the browser's autofill, such as country, set on the hidden input.

props.name: size
props.description: The control height, sm, md or lg; without it, the container's, and else md. sm is for a field with its label hidden.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label in the field, where it rests while the field is empty and floats into the outline while the field has focus or a value. Set false for a field whose purpose is clear without it, such as a search in a toolbar: the label still names the field for assistive technology, and a placeholder gives the visible guidance.

Sheet.description: A panel that slides in over the page from an edge of the window, for filters, details, an inspector or choices: a side sheet from the end or the start edge, or a bottom sheet. It is a modal by default, which traps focus and returns it on close, or beside the page with modal false. A side sheet takes the whole width of a compact window, and a finger's swipe toward its edge closes it; a mouse or a pen never swipes it. With `resizable`, people resize it by its inner edge, with the same handle as between Panes. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the sheet's surface.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the sheet is open, for a sheet the application controls with onOpenChange.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether a sheet the application doesn't control is open on the first render.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the requested state, and why, when the sheet asks to open or close: from the trigger, Escape, an outside press, the close button, a swipe of a finger toward its edge or a DialogClose. Not called for a dismissal that pending blocks.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element that opens the sheet, such as a Button. It reports the sheet it opens, and focus returns to it on close. Omit it for a sheet the application opens with open.

props.name: side
props.description: The edge of the window the sheet slides in from: end, the right in left-to-right text, or start, the left, as a side sheet as tall as the window; or bottom, as a bottom sheet as wide as the window up to 40 rem and as tall as its content. start and end follow the text direction, so they are mirrored in right-to-left text.

props.name: title
props.description: The sheet's heading and accessible name, such as Filters. Without one, name the sheet with aria-label.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The sheet's accessible name where it has no visible title.

props.name: description
props.description: Muted text under the title that describes the sheet to assistive technology too.

props.name: children
props.description: The content under the heading, such as filters, details or choices. It scrolls.

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions at the end of the content, such as Apply, with the primary action last. While the sheet is pending, the last one shows it, where it is a Button that sets no pending of its own.

props.name: closeButton
props.description: Whether the sheet shows its close button, an IconButton with a cross at the end of the heading. Leave it out only where the sheet holds another control that closes it.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name.

props.name: width
props.description: A side sheet's width: md, 24 rem, for details and filters; lg, 44 rem, for content-heavy panels such as tables and comparisons; or any CSS length, such as min(20rem, 100% - 2rem). md takes the whole width of a compact window, lg of a compact or medium one, where the page beside it would be a sliver. A number is a width in rem: with `resizable`, the width the application controls with onWidthChange, while a CSS length is ignored, and warned of while developing: the sheet starts at `defaultWidth`. A bottom sheet ignores it.

props.name: resizable
props.description: Lets people resize a side sheet by its inner edge, the one toward the page: a handle there that the pointer drags and the arrow keys move, between `minWidth` and `maxWidth` and never wider than the window, which a double click returns to `defaultWidth`. The sheet is then as wide as it at every window width. A bottom sheet ignores it.

props.name: defaultWidth
props.description: The width in rem a `resizable` side sheet starts at until people resize it, and that a double click on the handle returns it to.

props.name: onWidthChange
props.description: Receives each new width of a `resizable` side sheet, in rem: while dragging with committed false, and with committed true as a drag ends, a key moves the handle or a double click resets it. Store the committed width to keep it, and pass it back as `width`.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: The smallest width of a `resizable` side sheet, in rem.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: The largest width of a `resizable` side sheet, in rem; it never takes more than the window.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: The resize handle's name.

props.name: modal
props.description: true traps focus in the sheet over a backdrop, hides the page from assistive technology, blocks presses on it and locks its scroll. false leaves the page usable beside the sheet, for an inspector; it then closes when focus or a press goes outside it, unless disablePointerDismissal.

props.name: disablePointerDismissal
props.description: Keep the sheet open on presses outside it, and a non-modal sheet also when focus moves outside, such as an inspector beside the page it inspects. Escape and the close buttons still close it.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: The element to focus when the sheet opens, as a ref or a function of how it was opened. By default focus moves to the first element inside that takes Tab, such as the close button, or to the sheet itself when opened by touch or when nothing inside takes focus.

props.name: finalFocus
props.description: The element to focus when the sheet closes, as a ref or a function of how it closed, such as the main content after a navigation. By default focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus when it opened.

props.name: pending
props.description: Work started from the sheet is in progress: Escape, outside presses, swipes and the close button cannot dismiss it until pending returns to false. The close button and every DialogClose inside are disabled, the primary action, the last of actions, shows it pending, and the sheet reports busy.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

Slider.description: A value in a range, as a field: as tall as the fields and with their corners, so it sits in a form among them, with its label inside at the start, its value at the end and a fill from the start that shows it. Pressing or dragging anywhere in it chooses a value, and so do the arrow keys. At rest it shows its text, its fill and a quiet handle at the value; the handle at full strength and faint ticks at its steps appear under the pointer and while it is pressed, and go once it is released, and the handle alone shows with keyboard focus. An optional description sits below it.

props.name: label
props.description: The value's name, inside the slider at its start, such as Opacity. It names the slider.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the slider, such as what the value applies to, linked to the slider as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the slider that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the slider is invalid (aria-invalid), with the error color's edge, and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of a controlled slider; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value an uncontrolled slider starts with; a native form reset returns to it.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value while it changes, by dragging, pressing the track or with the keyboard, as often as the thumb moves.

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.description: Receives the value once a change is complete: when the thumb is released or the track pressed, and after each key. Use it for work that runs once per change, such as saving.

props.name: min
props.description: The lowest value, at the start of the track.

props.name: max
props.description: The highest value, at the end of the track.

props.name: step
props.description: The distance between the values the slider can take, counted from min; an arrow key moves by it.

props.name: largeStep
props.default: a tenth of the range in whole steps, at least one step
props.description: The change of Page Up, Page Down and an arrow key with Shift.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: The value as people read it at the slider's end and assistive technology announces it, such as (value) => `${value}%`. Without it, the number shows in the locale.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the shown number: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dim the slider; it can't be focused or moved, and forms leave it out.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the value with a form under this name.

props.name: form
props.description: The id of a form the slider belongs to when it sits outside of it.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native range input, which holds the value and takes focus, as a field's ref reaches its input: for example to focus it, or for a form library to register it. className, style and the other native props go to the root.

Spinner.description: Work of unknown length in a small area, such as a panel that is updating: an arc in the control blue that turns, and keeps turning slowly with a reduced-motion preference. With a label it is a progress bar named by it; without one it is hidden from assistive technology. With showLabel it is a status line with its label beside it, for loading with no known shape. The hook --env-spinner-color recolors it, such as to a button's label color.

props.name: label
props.description: The work it stands for, such as Refreshing members or Loading project. Alone it names the spinner as a progress bar for assistive technology; with showLabel it shows beside it. Leave it out where a busy control or region already says so; the spinner is then hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label beside the spinner, for loading with no known shape, such as search results: a status line, marked busy, that centers the spinner and its label in its row. Without a label it says Loading in the provider's language, from EnvUIProvider's messages.common.loading.

props.name: size
props.description: sm, 1 rem, inside controls and beside a line of text; md, 1.5 rem, beside a heading or in a panel; or lg, 3 rem, in the middle of a region whose content is on its way.

Surface.description: A container with a background, an inset and corners, but no layout of its own: spacing between its children, alignment and behavior come from what it holds, such as a Column. Card and other containers build on it.

props.name: background
props.description: The fill: default, the background of panes and side regions; muted, the background of rows; page, the page background; raised, a block that stands out on a pane; or recessed, a well on the page that what it holds rises out of: a shade deeper than it in dark, and lighter than it and the panes in light.

props.name: padding
props.default: 1.25 rem in narrow windows, growing to 1.5 rem from 50 rem wide
props.description: The inset on every side, as a step of the spacing scale, from 1 (0.25 rem) to 9 (4 rem), such as 5 for 1.5 rem; 0 removes it. Without it, the inset follows the window's width.

props.name: radius
props.description: The corner radius: xl, the large 1.75 rem corners of panes; sm, 0.5 rem for small blocks; full, fully rounded ends for a toolbar or a bar of filters; or none, square, for a region that meets the edges of its container.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render the surface as, for its meaning, such as render={<section />}, or another component to render it onto without a wrapper, such as a Column that lays out its content: the surface's class, style and attributes merge into its props. It must forward native props and refs. A div by default.

props.name: ref
props.description: The rendered element, a div by default. Its type is the element type parameter, which a ref passed in sets: a ref to the element that render makes, such as useRef<HTMLElement>(null) with render={<section />}, type-checks, and `SurfaceProps['ref']` is a ref to the default element, so a wrapper can forward it to one.

Switch.description: An on/off setting that takes effect at once: a native checkbox with the switch role, drawn as a track and a thumb, with its label beside it.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native checkbox with the switch role, so that a form library can register it and focus it; the other native props, such as name, reach it too.

props.name: className
props.description: The switch's class, on its root element, the label around the track and the text.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the root element.

props.name: label
props.description: The setting the switch turns on or off, such as Show completed tasks, beside the track. It names the switch, stays the same in both states, and pressing it toggles the switch too. Without it, name the switch with aria-label or aria-labelledby.

props.name: description
props.description: A short, muted line under the label, such as what the option changes. It is part of the switch's label, so it is read with its name.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether a controlled switch is on; update it from onCheckedChange.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled switch starts on; a native form reset returns it to this state.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Receives the new state each time people turn the switch on or off.

Table.Body.description: The data rows of a table, a native tbody, separated by hairlines.

Table.Cell.description: A data cell, a native td, with a label that names its value while rows stack.

props.name: label
props.description: The column's name, shown before the value while a table with narrowLayout="stack" stacks its rows. Assistive technology reads the column header instead.

props.name: align
props.description: Aligns the content with the start or the end of the cell.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures aligned to the end, for numbers that compare down a column. In a sortable header the arrow comes before the label, so the label lines up with the numbers.

props.name: nowrap
props.description: Keeps the content on one line. In a table with set column widths, content that doesn't fit ends with an ellipsis.

Table.Head.description: The header rows of a table, a native thead, which hold the column headers.

Table.HeaderCell.description: A header cell, a native th that heads its column, or its row with scope="row". With onSortChange it sorts its column; in a table with resizable columns it holds the column's resize handle.

props.name: sortDirection
props.description: The column's sort order: aria-sort on the header and the arrow in its sort button. Use it with onSortChange; without it only sets aria-sort.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: The header becomes a button across the cell that asks the application to sort the rows by this column, with the order pressing it asks for: descending while the column is sorted ascending, ascending otherwise. The application sorts the rows and sets sortDirection.

props.name: sortLabel
props.default: '{header} sort {next order}', from EnvUIProvider's messages.table.sortAscending and sortDescending
props.description: Accessible name of the sort button, which says what pressing it does: the header's name followed by "sort ascending", or by "sort descending" while the column is sorted ascending.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the column's resize handle, "Resize" followed by the header's name.

props.name: align
props.description: Aligns the content with the start or the end of the cell.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures aligned to the end, for numbers that compare down a column. In a sortable header the arrow comes before the label, so the label lines up with the numbers.

props.name: nowrap
props.description: Keeps the content on one line. In a table with set column widths, content that doesn't fit ends with an ellipsis.

Table.Root.description: A semantic data table on a rounded surface, in a focusable region that scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the table and its scroll region when there is no caption. A table needs a caption, an aria-label or an aria-labelledby, which names its region too.

props.name: caption
props.description: A visible caption above the rows that names the table and its scroll region, in place of aria-label or aria-labelledby. Under a sticky header it scrolls away with the rows.

props.name: density
props.description: How tightly the rows pack: xs, sm, md or lg changes only the cells' block padding, never the text. Buttons, icon buttons and fields in the cells take the small control height in every density, unless they set a size.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: The header row stays at the top of the region while the rows scroll beneath it. The region then scrolls vertically too, so give it a height through regionClassName or the surrounding layout.

props.name: regionClassName
props.description: Class of the scroll region around the table, for example to limit its height.

props.name: narrowLayout
props.description: What the table does when its region is narrower than stackBelow: scroll keeps the columns and scrolls sideways; stack shows each body row as a block that starts with its first cell, followed by the other cells with their labels. The header row is then visually hidden. A container query on the region decides it, so the server's markup and the first paint already stack; a stacking region fills the width its context gives it.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: The region width below which a table with narrowLayout="stack" stacks its rows: a CSS length such as 60rem or 480px, or a number of rem, such as 40 or "40", as PanelDock's. Wide tables, such as seven sortable columns, need more.

props.name: onStackedChange
props.description: Called with true when the rows stack and with false when the columns return, as the table reads its layout once it is in the document, for example to show another sort control while the header row is hidden; a table that leaves while its rows stack reports false. The region has data-stacked from then on while the rows stack; style stacked rows with a container query on env-table, which applies before hydration, rather than through it.

props.name: columnWidths
props.description: Column widths in percent of the table width, in column order and adding up to 100, for widths the application controls with onColumnWidthsChange. Set widths fix the columns: long words wrap and nowrap cells end with an ellipsis.

props.name: defaultColumnWidths
props.description: Starting column widths, in percent, when the table owns them; other defaults start them over. Double-clicking a resize handle restores them, or else the widths a controlled table started with.

props.name: onColumnWidthsChange
props.description: Called with every column's width when people resize a column: while dragging a handle with committed false, and with committed true as a drag ends, a key moves it or a double click resets the widths.

props.name: minColumnWidths
props.description: Smallest width of each column in percent, in column order, or one value for every column.

props.name: resizableColumns
props.description: People can resize the columns with a handle at the end of each header cell but the last, which moves the boundary to the next column and keeps the table's width. Needs columnWidths or defaultColumnWidths.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

Table.Row.description: A row of a table, a native tr, which can highlight on hover or be selected.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The row highlights on hover and while focus is inside it, for rows that open something through a link or button in a cell. It adds no behavior of its own.

props.name: selected
props.description: The row is selected: it reports aria-selected and takes the selection colors, with a bar at its start. Pass false to the other rows of a table whose rows can be selected; unset, a row reports no selection state.

TableOfContents.description: The page's sections as links, nested by level, with the one the reader is in marked as they scroll: the headings in a container by default, or sections of your own.

props.name: items
props.description: The sections to list, nested through `children`, each leading to the element with its `id`: a heading or any other part of the page, under a label of your own. Without it, the component lists the headings it finds in `container`, after it mounts.

props.name: container
props.default: The page's `main` element, or the body without one
props.description: Where to find the headings, without `items`: an element's ref or a CSS selector.

props.name: levels
props.description: The heading levels to list, without `items`. A heading nests under the one above it of a lower level. A heading without an id gets one from its words.

props.name: filter
props.description: Leaves out the headings it returns false for, without `items`, such as an example's own.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The accessible name of the navigation landmark.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the `nav` element.

Tabs.description: Switches between panels of related content in one place: a rail of the buttons you supply, each a tab linked to its panel, with selection from the keyboard and panels that fade as they change. Every tab is a text tab, the selected one in the accent color with an indicator under it.

props.name: items
props.description: The tabs in order, each with its value, its label or button, and its panel content.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The tab list's accessible name, such as Project views.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected tab's value, for controlled tabs; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The tab that uncontrolled tabs start on.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the tab people select, by pressing it or from the keyboard.

props.name: activation
props.description: automatic selects a tab as the arrow keys move focus to it; manual only moves focus, and Enter or Space selects, for panels that take a moment to show.

props.name: orientation
props.description: horizontal puts the tabs in a row, moved through with the left and right arrow keys; vertical in a column, with the up and down arrow keys. The panels stay below the list either way.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description: Keep the panels of unselected tabs mounted and hidden, so their state, such as a draft or a scroll position, survives switching; otherwise a panel unmounts once it has faded out.

props.name: renderList
props.description: Places the tab list in a layout of your own, such as beside a heading: it receives the list and returns what to render in its place, with the list in it once. The panels stay below.

props.name: listClassName
props.description: A class for the tab list, the rail that holds the tabs.

props.name: panelClassName
props.description: A class for every panel.

props.name: fill
props.description: The selected panel takes the height left below the list, for content that fills a region, such as a canvas; give the tabs a height, for example as a flex child.

props.name: size
props.description: The rail's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. The tabs inside are a little shorter. lg gives tabs as tall as md buttons; sm suits a toolbar or a bar, beside a SegmentedControl or buttons of size sm.

Text.description: Semantic native text with typography and color from the shared token scale.

props.name: variant
props.description: The text style: display for a page's introduction, body for running text, headline for a page's heading, title for a section's, body-sm for supporting text and caption for the smallest notes. body-sm and caption are muted unless emphasis says otherwise.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: How strong the text is: default, the text color; muted, for supporting text; subtle, the weakest, for text that should recede, such as a hint beside a value.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<h2 />} for a heading or render={<span />} inside a line; a p by default. The text's class and attributes merge into its props.

props.name: ref
props.description: The rendered element, a p by default. Its type is the element type parameter, which a ref passed in sets: a ref to the element that render makes, such as useRef<HTMLElement>(null) with render={<section />}, type-checks, and `TextProps['ref']` is a ref to the default element, so a wrapper can forward it to one.

TextField.description: A labelled single-line text input: a native input with a floating label, a description and an error, at the control height in an outline or ghost look, with an optional start icon, end action, prefix and suffix.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native input, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-text-field.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value as people type, after the native onChange.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look: outline, a thin border its label floats into, or ghost, a faint fill, for a search at the top of a sidebar or a list.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: A decorative icon at the start of the field, such as Search or Mail.

props.name: endAction
props.description: A control at the end of the field, such as an IconButton that reveals or copies the value; name it with aria-label. A button that sets no variant takes ghost here.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label in the field, where it rests while the field is empty and floats into the outline while the field has focus or a value. Set false for a field whose purpose is clear without it, such as a search in a toolbar: the label still names the field for assistive technology, and a placeholder gives the visible guidance.

props.name: size
props.description: The control height, sm, md or lg; without it, the container's, and else md. sm is for a field with its label hidden.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text before the value, such as the start of an address. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text after the value, such as a unit. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

Textarea.description: A labelled text area for text over several lines: a native textarea in the text field's frame, at a fixed height that scrolls and resizes from its bottom edge, or growing with its content.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native text area, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field, env-text-field and env-textarea.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element, such as its width in a row.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look, as TextField's: outline or ghost. A text area is always tall, with its label resting at the top.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the text as people type, after the native onChange.

props.name: sizing
props.description: How the height follows the text: fixed keeps its height, scrolls and resizes from the bottom edge, by dragging it or with the arrow keys; content grows and shrinks with the text.

props.name: rows
props.description: The lines the field shows: with fixed sizing, its height in rows, which resizes down to them or to 7.5 rem, whichever is less; with content sizing, the lines it starts at and shrinks back to. Without rows, both start at 7.5 rem.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

Theme.description: An explicit, scoped theme: a color scheme, a contrast and a scale, which nested Themes and envUI's popups keep. Theme preference and persistence belong to the app.

props.name: theme
props.description: The color scheme.

props.name: contrast
props.description: `high` for the high-contrast colors; `standard` keeps the standard ones even while the system asks for more contrast; `system` follows `prefers-contrast: more`. Defaults to the contrast of the enclosing Theme, and to `system` outside any. It wins over a `data-env-contrast` attribute passed to the Theme; left out, such an attribute of `high` or `standard` sets the contrast, for the boundary, its nested Themes and its popups alike.

props.name: scale
props.description: The app scale of everything inside: comfortable, compact, or `system`, which is compact under a fine pointer and comfortable on touch, chosen by the stylesheet. Use one scale per app or window, and another only on a Theme around a whole region, such as a docked inspector. Defaults to the scale of the enclosing Theme, and to `system` outside any. It wins over a `data-env-scale` attribute passed to the Theme.

ThemeMenuRadioGroup.description: The theme choice for a Menu: System, Light and Dark as radio items. Inside a ThemePreferenceProvider it shows and stores the provider's preference; value and onValueChange connect it to a theme the application stores itself.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen preference: system, light or dark.

props.name: onValueChange
props.default: the nearest ThemePreferenceProvider's setPreference, which stores the choice
props.description: Called with the preference chosen, for an application that stores the theme itself.

props.name: label
props.description: A small heading above the choices, which names the group. Leave it out inside a submenu, which its row already names.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of a heading elsewhere in the menu that names the group, in place of label.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Close the menu after a choice. Off by default, so people see the theme change with the menu still open.

ThemePreferenceProvider.description: Owns the theme preference: persistence, the system theme and document-root theming.

props.name: children
props.description: The application, or the part of it that the preference themes.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: localStorage key; match the bootstrap script's. Defaults to "env-theme".

props.name: defaultPreference
props.description: Used when nothing is stored. Defaults to "system".

props.name: applyToDocument
props.description: Theme the document root as well as this subtree (default). Root theming covers the page background, native controls, portals rendered by other libraries and the content of every theme-color meta tag, which takes the canvas color. One provider per document applies to it: pass false to any other, nested in it or beside it. In development, envUI reports two providers that both apply.

props.name: contrast
props.description: Contrast of the Theme boundary around the children, and of the document root with applyToDocument: high, standard, or system to follow `prefers-contrast: more`, as on Theme. Defaults to the contrast of an enclosing Theme; outside any, a provider applying to the document gives its boundary a contrast the page set on the root, and otherwise system. With system, the provider removes from the root only a contrast that envUI wrote and the page left unchanged: a provider, this one or one before it, or the bootstrap script. Pass a contrast that is fixed for the application to createThemeBootstrapScript too, so the root has it before the first paint.

props.name: scale
props.description: The app scale, comfortable, compact or `system` (compact under a fine pointer, comfortable on touch), as on Theme: of the Theme boundary around the children, and, marked as envUI's own, of the document root with applyToDocument. Without it, the boundary takes the scale of an enclosing Theme; outside any, a provider applying to the document gives its boundary a scale the page set on the root, so the application, the page and its portals share it, and otherwise `system`. The root keeps a scale the page set but drops one that envUI wrote and the page left unchanged. Pass the same scale to createThemeBootstrapScript so the root has it before the first paint.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the Theme boundary around the children.

ThemeToggle.description: Switches between the light and dark themes and stores the choice.

props.name: size
props.description: As Button's: the height, and the width, of the square button.

props.name: variant
props.description: The emphasis, as Button's. Without it, the button takes the variant its container gives, such as ghost in a toolbar, and else secondary.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning, as Button's.

props.name: pending
props.description: As Button's: a spinner replaces the icon while the work runs.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The button's name; without it, Switch to dark theme or Switch to light theme, or EnvUIProvider's messages.themePreference.

TimePicker.description: A field for a time of day that shows the value in the reader's locale and opens wheels of its hours, minutes every `minuteStep` and, on a 12-hour clock, the day's halves to choose it.

props.name: value
props.description: The value: a time of day as HH:mm on the 24-hour clock. null, or an empty string, for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value an uncontrolled field starts with, and that a form reset restores; none by default.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the new value as HH:mm, or null once the field is cleared.

props.name: min
props.description: The earliest time, as HH:mm; earlier times are unavailable.

props.name: max
props.description: The latest time, as HH:mm; later times are unavailable.

props.name: minuteStep
props.description: The minutes between the times the list offers, from 1 to 60. A value between them still shows in the list, in its place.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the shown value and the list's times, with its own 12- or 24-hour clock: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's.

props.name: formatOptions
props.description: How the field shows the value: Intl.DateTimeFormat options, by default the short time style.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the field's clear button and text of the popup's.

props.name: nowLabel
props.description: The popup's shortcut to the current time.

props.name: ref
props.description: The field's button, which shows the value and opens the popup.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element.

props.name: name
props.description: The name the value is submitted under with a form.

props.name: required
props.description: A value is needed: an empty field keeps its form from submitting and takes focus.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: The value can be read and focused but not changed.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while the field is empty and its label floats or is hidden.

props.name: size
props.description: The control height, sm, md or lg; without it, the container's, and else md. sm is for a field with its label hidden.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label inside the field, where it floats into the outline while the field has a value, focus or its popup open. Set false for a field whose purpose is clear without it.

props.name: clearable
props.description: A clear button in the field and in the popup removes the value.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popup is open; with `onOpenChange` it controls it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled popup starts open; closed by default.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new state, and why, when the popup opens or closes.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

ToastProvider.description: Hosts the notifications that useToast shows: brief feedback at the edge of the window, announced and dismissed after a few seconds or by people. Put one near the root of the application; it renders a region for each placement in a portal, in the theme of the place it is rendered.

props.name: children
props.description: The application, or the part of it whose components call useToast.

props.name: defaultPlacement
props.description: Where notifications show unless show names a placement: bottom-end, stacking upward from the bottom corner at the end of the line, or top-center, stacking downward from the top.

props.name: limit
props.description: How many notifications each placement shows at once, a positive integer. The newest stay visible; older ones wait behind a count of hidden notifications and come back as newer ones close. Danger notifications always show, and take their places first.

Toolbar.Button.description: An icon-only button of a toolbar, named by its label, which a tooltip shows; disabled, it leaves the arrow keys' path.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon, such as FormatBold.

props.name: label
props.description: The action's name, such as Bold: assistive technology announces it, and the tooltip shows it on hover and focus.

props.name: pressed
props.description: For a button that turns something on and off, such as Bold: whether it is on. It is announced as pressed and drawn selected. Leave it out for a button that acts once, such as Undo.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: The keyboard shortcut that does the same, such as Ctrl+B, with keys joined by +: the tooltip shows it, and aria-keyshortcuts announces it, in ARIA's key names, such as Control+B. A sequence, such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+B, shows its keys without the attribute, as in Menu.

props.name: variant
props.description: As Button's; ghost by default, from the toolbar.

props.name: tone
props.description: As Button's: danger for an action that destroys, such as Delete, so it keeps its warning without a label.

props.name: pending
props.description: As Button's: a spinner replaces the icon while the work runs.

Toolbar.Group.description: Controls of a toolbar that belong together, such as the text styles.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the group, such as Text style, where its controls belong together.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control in the group.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element to render the group as, such as a ButtonGroup.

Toolbar.Link.description: An icon-only link of a toolbar, named by its label, which a tooltip shows. In a disabled toolbar or group it has no destination: it reports aria-disabled, leaves the arrow keys' path and has no tooltip, as a disabled button does.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination, through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon, such as Help.

props.name: label
props.description: The destination's name, which assistive technology announces and the tooltip shows.

Toolbar.Root.description: A row, or a column, of controls for one subject, such as a text editor's formatting: one tab stop, with the arrow keys moving between its controls (the APG toolbar pattern). Buttons the application puts inside take the ghost variant unless they set another.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the toolbar for assistive technology, such as Formatting.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The direction the controls run in, and which arrow keys move between them.

props.name: size
props.description: The height of the buttons inside, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the control height of the container.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control inside.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: Whether the arrow keys move from the last control to the first and back.

props.name: tooltipDelay
props.description: Milliseconds the pointer rests on a button or link before its tooltip opens, as Tooltip's delay; keyboard focus opens it at once. 0 shows every name at once, for a toolbar people scan by pointing, such as a canvas's view controls.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element to render the toolbar as, such as a ButtonGroup that connects its buttons; the toolbar's class, attributes and keyboard handling merge into its props.

props.name: children
props.description: The controls: Toolbar.Button, Toolbar.Link, Toolbar.Group and Toolbar.Separator.

Toolbar.Separator.description: A line between groups of a toolbar's controls, across the toolbar's direction.

Tooltip.description: A short label beside a control, shown while the pointer rests on it or it has keyboard focus, such as an icon-only button's name or why a control is disabled. It closes on Esc and when the control is pressed, and stays closed while the control's own popup, such as a menu, is open. Native props and ref go to the control, so a Tooltip can be the trigger of a Menu.Root or Popover; popupClassName styles the tooltip's popup.

props.name: content
props.description: What the tooltip shows: a short, supplementary text, such as an icon-only control's name or why a control is disabled. While it is open, a control with a name of its own is described by it (aria-describedby); never the only place essential information appears.

props.name: children
props.description: The one control it describes, such as an IconButton, which takes the trigger's props and ref, and the Tooltip's own native props and ref. Around a Menu.Root, Popover, Dialog, Sheet or ConfirmDialog, the tooltip describes their `trigger`; around a HoverCard, it shows nothing. A disabled control is wrapped in an element that hovering opens the tooltip on. Around a button, link, tab or menu item, it is focusable and carries the control's name, role and state, reported disabled, so keyboard focus opens it too. One element: text, a Fragment or a component that doesn't pass the ref on to its element gets no tooltip, and says so while developing. Text, such as a focusable span or Text that holds text, takes a quiet dotted underline, env-hover-detail.

props.name: ref
props.description: The control's ref, as the Tooltip passes its props on to the control, such as when the Tooltip is the `trigger` of a Menu.Root or Popover, which give their trigger a ref.

props.name: popupClassName
props.description: Class of the tooltip's popup, beside env-tooltip.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of the control it opens on: top, bottom, left, right, or inline-start and inline-end, which follow the text direction. Where the window has no room, it flips to the other side.

props.name: align
props.description: How the tooltip lines up with the control along that side: its start, center or end.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds the pointer rests on the control before the tooltip opens; keyboard focus opens it at once.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the tooltip starts open, such as in a picture of the interface; it then closes as an opened one does.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the tooltip shows, for a tooltip the application controls with onOpenChange, such as one a step of a tour opens.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Receives the requested state, and why, as the pointer rests on the control or leaves it, focus reaches or leaves it, it is pressed or Esc closes the tooltip.

TopBar.description: The bar at the top of an application or a screen: start content, such as a navigation button or the application's mark, the title, which truncates first, and the actions at the end, in one row that never wraps, at the top bar height. It can stick to the top as the page scrolls, show page progress along its bottom edge, or be the window's own title bar.

props.name: start
props.description: Content before the title, at the inline start: a navigation IconButton, such as one that opens a navigation drawer, a back IconButton, or the application's mark.

props.name: title
props.description: The title, such as the application's or the section's name. It truncates before the start content and the actions shrink. It is no heading: the page's own heading is its PageHeader's.

props.name: actions
props.description: The actions at the inline end, such as a search trigger, a theme toggle and an account menu, in the order people read them.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Keeps the bar at the top of the scrolling area as it scrolls, for a bar in a page whose document scrolls. In a Scaffold's top bar region it is unneeded: the body scrolls under it.

props.name: titleBar
props.description: The bar is the window's title bar, in an installed web app or a desktop shell that draws its own (the Window Controls Overlay): empty space drags the window, it leaves room for the window controls the system draws, the title is centered, and its controls are small, with buttons that set no variant ghost. Put it in a Scaffold with topBarSpan="full".

props.name: background
props.description: The bar's background, named as Surface's and Card's: default, the navigation's background, the default surface color, as a plain rectangle; page, the page's background, so it sits on the page. On a surface, such as a Sheet, both take the surface's color. Set it on its own, such as a TopBar with page over a NavigationDrawer with its background.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows page progress along the bar's bottom edge, such as while the next page loads.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: The progress bar's name.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, such as render={<header />} for a bar outside a Scaffold, which then is the page's banner; a div by default, as Scaffold's top bar region is the banner.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

Tree.description: A virtualized tree of rows for large hierarchies such as file trees. The application passes the visible rows and owns expansion and selection; the tree owns focus, keyboard navigation and scrolling. It fills its parent's height, scrolls itself and renders only the rows in view.

props.name: items
props.description: The visible rows in order, flattened: an expanded row is followed by its visible descendants. The application owns expansion; collapsing a row removes its descendants from items.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The tree's accessible name, such as Files.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected row's value: it takes the navigation selection colors and scrolls into view when it changes. The application sets it, usually from onAction.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Called when people open a row: with preview true on a single click and Space, and false on a double click and Enter. Expandable rows call it too, and disabled rows don't.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Called with the row and its new state from a press on its chevron, the right arrow key on a collapsed row and the left arrow key on an expanded one, mirrored in right-to-left text. The application updates items.

props.name: contextMenu
props.description: Menu items for the row people right-click, or press Shift+F10 or the Menu key on, or for the tree's empty area when the item is null. Without it, the browser's own context menu stays.

props.name: contextMenuLabel
props.description: The context menu's accessible name.

props.name: density
props.description: How tightly the rows pack: xs, sm, md or lg changes only their block padding, never the text or the icons. In the comfortable scale sm rows are 1.75 rem tall and md rows 2.25 rem. Under a coarse pointer every row is at least 2.75 rem.

avatarHue.description: The hue a name gives an avatar: the same name always gives the same hue, on every page and in every session, and different names spread across the hues. Letter case and surrounding spaces do not count.

countDiffLines.description: How many lines a change adds and removes, as a DiffStat shows them.
countDiffLines.signature: (before: string, after: string, filename?: string): { additions: number; deletions: number; }

createRichTextExtensions.description: The Tiptap extensions RichTextEditor and RichText share: formatting, lists and task lists, tables, safe links and images, Markdown with raw HTML kept as text, a placeholder and references. options.extensions are added after them, for other Tiptap integrations that need the same schema.

createThemeBootstrapScript.description: Inline script for the document head. It themes the root element before the first paint, so a saved or system dark theme does not flash light while the application loads, and a high or standard contrast applies from the start.
createThemeBootstrapScript.signature: ({ storageKey, defaultPreference, contrast, scale, }?: ThemeBootstrapOptions): string

formatRelativeTime.description: A moment as text relative to another, by default the current time, such as "in 2 days", "3 hours ago" or "just now", through Intl.RelativeTimeFormat. An invalid moment gives an empty string; an invalid now is ignored, as by RelativeTime, for the current time.

installDevMode.description: Installs dev mode: `window.envui.layout` with `describe()`, `check()` and `at()`, a button in the corner and Alt+Shift+D, which open the page in a new tab with the 3D view and the inspector over the whole window. Closing that tab ends dev mode; the page it came from stays as it was. Load it in development only, so production builds contain none of it: if (import.meta.env.DEV) { void import('@envsemble/envui/dev').then(({ installDevMode }) => installDevMode()); } Calling it again returns the dev mode already installed, until it is uninstalled.

isPlaceholder.description: Whether an item is one of the stand-ins that `placeholders()` returns, by its id, so it holds after the items are serialized, such as from a server component to a client one. It narrows the type: `isPlaceholder(item) ? <Skeleton /> : item.name`, where item.name is the item's own.

placeholders.description: Stand-in items for data that is loading, so the page renders its normal components over them while a surface around them is a skeleton: `items ?? placeholders<Project>(3)`. Each item has only an `id`, `envui-placeholder-0`, `envui-placeholder-1` and so on, for keys; its other fields are undefined, which the type says, and the components render missing text as bars of a default length for its text style.

readPanesWidth.description: The width Panes keeps under its `persist` key, read from a Cookie header, such as the request's on the server, or from `document.cookie`. Render Panes.Root with it as `persistedWidth`, on the server and in the browser alike, so the server's markup has the width people chose and nothing moves as the page hydrates: <Panes.Root persist="inbox" persistedWidth={readPanesWidth(cookieHeader, 'inbox')}> Returns undefined where no width is kept under the key.
readPanesWidth.signature: (cookies: string | null | undefined, key: string): number | undefined

useContainerSize.description: The size of an element, kept up to date as it changes: its inline and block size in CSS pixels, along its writing mode, from a ResizeObserver. It is undefined on the server and until the element is measured, which happens before the browser paints it; an element that stops being rendered, such as one in a hidden tab panel, keeps its last size until it shows again. Pass a ref object, read once the element mounts, or the element itself, such as one kept in state by a callback ref. Prefer a container query (`@container`) where only styles change. const panel = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null); const size = useContainerSize(panel); const narrow = size !== undefined && size.inlineSize < 640;
useContainerSize.signature: <T extends Element>(target: RefObject<T | null> | T | null, options?: ContainerSizeOptions): ContainerSize | undefined

useLocale.description: The locale of the nearest EnvUIProvider, for formatting in step with envUI, or undefined where no provider sets one: the runtime's locale applies then.

useModifierKey.description: The platform's modifier for shortcuts: ⌘ on Apple platforms, Ctrl elsewhere. The server and the first render in the browser give Ctrl, so the markup hydrates; an Apple browser then renders ⌘.

useSkeleton.description: Whether the component is inside a skeleton: a surface with `skeleton` around it. A component of the application's own reads it to give its skeleton a look of its own, such as a chart's.

useTheme.description: The theme of the nearest Theme, including across React portals: its color scheme, contrast and scale. A portal of the application's own takes it with `<Theme {...useTheme()}>`. A contrast of `system` leaves the choice to the stylesheet, which reads `prefers-contrast: more`, as a scale of `system` leaves it to `pointer: fine`.

useThemePreference.description: The theme preference from the nearest ThemePreferenceProvider.

useToast.description: Shows and dismisses notifications through the nearest ToastProvider: show, dismiss and clear. Throws outside a provider.
